title: Braided Eden and Ghost Genomes: Out of Africa, Archaic Admixture, and the Weakly Structured Stem of Human Origins — From Wolpoff's Multiregional Continuity vs. strict zero-admixture replacement to leaky Out-of-Africa synthesis; Cann, Stoneking & Wilson's 1987 mtDNA coalescent tree & Stringer & Andrews's 1988 fossil-genetic synthesis; Green et al.'s 2010 Neanderthal ABBA-BABA shock (~2% Eurasian introgression) & Reich/Meyer's Denisova finger-bone genome (~5% Oceanian introgression + Tibetan EPAS1); Hublin's 315-ka Moroccan Jebel Irhoud crania & Ragsdale et al.'s 2023 weakly structured pan-African stem; coalescent vs. tract-length math & ancient-DNA field guide

teenKit.tldr: Humans didn't just burst out of a single African valley to replace everyone else; instead, our ancestors evolved across a vast, interconnected African continent and occasionally interbred with other human species like Neanderthals.
teenKit.whyItMatters: Unlocking our ancient DNA reveals that the ghosts of extinct human species still live inside our genomes today, influencing everything from our immune systems to how our bodies handle high altitudes.
keyTakeaways: The old debate pitted total replacement against global multiregionalism, but modern paleogenomics proved the real answer is a 'leaky' Out-of-Africa model.
Ancient DNA extraction from tiny fossils like a Denisovan pinky bone or Moroccan Jebel Irhoud tools revolutionized our understanding of deep human history.
Most non-Africans carry about two percent Neanderthal DNA, proving our ancestors mingled as they spread across the globe.

vocab.meaning: The fancy scientific term for when different human species, like Homo sapiens and Neanderthals, mated and had children together.
The single common female ancestor on the maternal side from whom all living humans inherited a specific loop of DNA.
A mathematical family tree that traces genetic traits backward in time until they merge at a single common ancestor.
The theory that early humans evolved across multiple connected regions within Africa rather than in just one isolated pocket.

quiz.question: What percentage of Neanderthal ancestry do most non-African humans carry in their genomes today?
quiz.explanation: Pioneering ancient DNA studies in 2010 revealed that non-African genomes contain roughly two percent Neanderthal introgression.

quiz.question: Where were the 315,000-year-old Jebel Irhoud fossils discovered, completely reshaping our view of early human history?
quiz.explanation: The Jebel Irhoud fossils were excavated from a site in Morocco, serving as a vital anchor for early Homo sapiens history.

quiz.question: What does the 'leaky Out-of-Africa' model suggest about human migration?
options: Humans migrated out of Africa and instantly wiped out every other hominin without contact.
Humans never left Africa until very recently.
Humans migrated out of Africa and interbred along the way with archaic groups like Neanderthals and Denisovans.
Humans originally evolved in Siberia and migrated south.
quiz.explanation: The leaky model bridges replacement and multiregionalism by showing modern humans left Africa while also mixing with regional archaic populations.
